name: Roti Canai with Dhal
description: Flaky, buttery Malaysian flatbread torn and dipped into a mild, turmeric-scented lentil dhal.
steps: Mix the plain flour, salt, egg, condensed milk and warm water into a soft sticky dough, then knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Divide the dough into 4 balls, coat each generously with ghee, put them in a dish, cover and rest for at least 1 hour (or overnight).
For the dhal, rinse the red lentils and simmer them in the water with turmeric for 20 minutes over medium-low heat until soft, stirring occasionally.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, curry leaves and curry powder and cook 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomato, cook 3 minutes until soft, then stir this mixture into the lentils and season with salt; keep warm.
On an oiled surface, stretch one dough ball as thin as paper with your hands, then fold it into a square or coil it into a spiral to trap the layers.
Cook each roti on a hot greased pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Clap the hot roti between your hands to fluff up the layers and serve at once with the dhal.
tips: Resting the oiled dough is what makes it stretch thin without tearing.
photo: A golden flaky roti canai torn open on a round plate beside a small bowl of yellow dhal topped with fried curry leaves.

name: Nasi Goreng
description: Smoky, sweet-savoury Indonesian fried rice topped with a crispy fried egg.
steps: Blend or pound the shallots, garlic, chillies and shrimp paste into a rough paste.
Slice the chicken thinly and season with a pinch of salt.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat, add the paste and stir-fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry 4 minutes; pour in the kecap manis and soy sauce and toss until evenly brown.
Stir in the sliced spring onions and taste for salt, then divide among plates.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the edges are crisp.
Top each plate with an egg, cucumber and tomato slices and fried shallots.
tips: Day-old cold rice fries better and will not turn mushy.
photo: A mound of dark glossy fried rice on a white plate topped with a crispy fried egg, with cucumber and tomato slices and golden fried shallots.

name: Bubur Ayam (Chicken Rice Porridge)
description: Silky rice porridge simmered in chicken broth and topped with shredded chicken, crunchy toppings and a soft egg.
steps: Put the chicken, water, sliced ginger, crushed garlic, bruised lemongrass, bay leaves and turmeric in a large pot and bring to the boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook the chicken for 25 minutes, skimming any foam, until tender.
Lift out the chicken, let it cool a little, then shred the meat with two forks.
Rinse the rice, add it to the strained broth and simmer on low for 35 minutes, stirring often, until it breaks down into a thick porridge.
Season with salt and white pepper, adding hot water if it becomes too thick.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water, then peel and halve them.
Ladle the porridge into bowls and top with shredded chicken, egg, spring onions, celery leaves and fried shallots.
Drizzle with soy sauce and serve hot.
tips: Stir the porridge regularly toward the end so it does not stick to the bottom.
photo: A deep white bowl of creamy porridge topped with shredded chicken, a halved egg, green spring onion and golden fried shallots.

name: Mee Goreng Mamak
description: Spicy, sweet Indian-Malaysian stir-fried yellow noodles with chicken, tofu, egg and a squeeze of lime.
steps: Rinse the noodles in hot water for 30 seconds to loosen them, then drain well.
Cut the chicken into thin slices, the tofu into cubes and the boiled potatoes into chunks.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat and fry the tofu until golden, about 3 minutes; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, fry the chopped garlic and shallots 1 minute, then the chilli paste for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir-fry 4 minutes until cooked through.
Push everything aside, crack in the eggs and scramble for 1 minute.
Add the noodles, potatoes, ketchup, soy sauce and kecap manis and toss over high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the choy sum and bean sprouts, toss 1 minute until just wilted, add the tofu back and serve with lime wedges.
tips: Keep the heat high and avoid overcrowding the wok so the noodles fry rather than steam.
photo: A glossy red-brown tangle of fried noodles on a plate with golden tofu cubes, greens, egg and a lime wedge on the side.

name: Curry Laksa
description: A rich, spicy coconut curry noodle soup with prawns, chicken, tofu puffs and fresh herbs.
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve them.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the laksa paste for 3 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Pour in the stock and coconut milk, add the sugar and fish sauce, and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Add the sliced chicken and cook 6 minutes, then add the prawns and tofu puffs and cook 3 minutes until the prawns turn pink.
Blanch the bean sprouts in boiling water for 20 seconds and place them with the noodles in four bowls.
Ladle the hot curry over the noodles and top with egg, coriander, mint and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Never boil the soup hard after adding coconut milk or it may split.
photo: A big bowl of orange curry broth with vermicelli, pink prawns, tofu puffs, a halved egg and a heap of green herbs.

name: Soto Ayam
description: A golden turmeric chicken soup with glass noodles, egg and a squeeze of lime, a staple across Indonesia.
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric and candlenuts into a smooth paste with a splash of water.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the paste for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the water, chicken, bruised lemongrass and lime leaves, bring to the boil and simmer 30 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in a separate pot for 15 minutes, then cut into chunks; boil the eggs for 8 minutes and peel.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat and season the broth with salt and white pepper.
Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 5 minutes and drain.
Place noodles, bean sprouts, chicken, potato and egg in bowls and ladle the hot broth over.
Top with spring onions and fried shallots and serve with lime wedges.
tips: Fry the chicken skin-side down briefly before boiling for extra flavour if you like.
photo: A bowl of bright yellow broth with shredded chicken, glass noodles, a halved egg, potato and fried shallot garnish, a lime wedge on the rim.

name: Gado-Gado
description: Blanched vegetables, tofu, potatoes and eggs drenched in a creamy, tangy peanut sauce.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender, then slice; boil the eggs for 8 minutes, peel and halve.
Blanch the green beans, cabbage, spinach and bean sprouts one after another in boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes each, then refresh in cold water and drain.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until golden on all sides.
For the sauce, grind or blend the peanuts, garlic, chillies and palm sugar to a coarse paste.
Add the tamarind, kecap manis, coconut milk and warm water and blend, then simmer 3 minutes over low heat; add salt to taste.
Arrange the vegetables, potatoes, tofu, egg and cucumber slices on a platter.
Pour the warm peanut sauce over and top with prawn crackers.
tips: Thin the sauce with warm water if it thickens as it cools.
photo: A colourful platter of green beans, cabbage, potato, tofu and halved eggs covered in thick peanut sauce with pink prawn crackers on top.

name: Pad Thai with Prawns
description: Chewy rice noodles stir-fried with prawns, egg and a tamarind sauce, finished with crushed peanuts and lime.
steps: Soak the noodles in warm water for 25 minutes until pliable but still firm, then drain.
Stir the tamarind, fish sauce and palm sugar in a small pan over low heat for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat, fry the diced tofu 3 minutes until golden, then add shallots and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the prawns and cook 2 minutes until pink, then push to one side.
Add the remaining oil, crack in the eggs and scramble 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss 3 minutes until the noodles absorb the sauce and soften.
Add half the bean sprouts and the chives, toss 30 seconds, then plate and top with crushed peanuts, chilli flakes, remaining sprouts and lime wedges.
tips: Cook in one or two batches; a crowded wok makes soggy noodles.
photo: A nest of orange-brown noodles with pink prawns on a plate, scattered with crushed peanuts, bean sprouts, chives and a lime wedge.

name: Salmon Onigiri
description: Hand-shaped Japanese rice triangles filled with flaky salted salmon and wrapped in crisp nori.
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs almost clear, then drain and soak it in the water for 20 minutes.
Bring to the boil in a lidded pot, then reduce to the lowest heat and cook 12 minutes; turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, season the salmon with 0.5 teaspoon salt and grill or pan-fry over medium heat for 4 minutes per side until cooked through.
Flake the salmon into small pieces, discarding the skin and bones, and mix with the soy sauce and vinegar.
Fluff the rice and let it cool until comfortable to touch.
Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt, take a quarter of the rice, press a hollow in the middle and add some salmon.
Cover with more rice and shape into a firm triangle with gentle pressure.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and wrap the base of each onigiri with a strip of nori.
tips: Wet hands with salted water so the rice does not stick.
photo: Four neat white rice triangles with black nori bands and sesame seeds, arranged on a small wooden board.

name: Egg Fried Rice
description: Fluffy wok-fried rice with scrambled egg, peas and spring onions, a Chinese home staple.
steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and finely dice the carrot; slice the spring onions, keeping whites and greens separate.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat, pour in the eggs and scramble 1 minute until just set, then remove.
Add the remaining oil, fry the garlic and spring onion whites for 20 seconds, then the carrot and peas for 2 minutes.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes, pressing out lumps, until piping hot.
Return the egg and add the soy sauce, white pepper and sesame oil, tossing for 1 minute.
Stir in the spring onion greens and taste for salt before serving.
tips: Use rice cooked the day before and chilled for the best texture.
photo: A bowl of golden fried rice flecked with yellow egg, green peas, orange carrot and spring onion.

name: Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce
description: Turmeric and lemongrass marinated chicken skewers grilled until charred, served with a rich peanut sauce.
steps: Soak the skewers in water for 30 minutes so they do not burn.
Blend the lemongrass, 3 shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander, cumin, 1 tablespoon palm sugar, 1 tablespoon oil and salt into a paste.
Cut the chicken into 2 cm strips, coat with the paste and marinate at least 1 hour.
For the sauce, blend the remaining shallot, dried chillies (soaked in hot water 10 minutes) and peanuts into a paste.
Fry the paste in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat for 4 minutes, add the water, coconut milk, tamarind and remaining sugar, and simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Thread the chicken onto skewers and grill over high heat or under a hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes per side, brushing with a little oil, until charred and cooked through.
Serve the satay with the warm peanut sauce, cucumber chunks and raw red onion.
tips: Thigh meat stays juicy; avoid breast unless you shorten the cooking time.
photo: A row of charred golden chicken skewers on a platter beside a bowl of glossy peanut sauce with cucumber and red onion chunks.

name: Ayam Masak Merah
description: Fried chicken simmered in a sweet, tangy and mildly spicy red tomato-chilli sauce, a festive Malay favourite.
steps: Rub the chicken with turmeric and salt and rest for 15 minutes.
Fry the chicken in hot oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side until golden; remove and drain, leaving 3 tablespoons oil in the pan.
Soak the dried chillies in hot water for 10 minutes, then blend with the shallots, garlic and ginger into a paste.
Fry the cinnamon, star anise and cardamom in the pan oil for 30 seconds, then add the paste and cook 6 minutes over medium heat until the oil separates.
Add the sliced onion, tomato puree, ketchup, tamarind, sugar and water and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the peas, cook 2 minutes and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Deseed some chillies if you want a milder sauce.
photo: Glossy red-glazed chicken pieces in a shallow dish with green peas and whole spices, served beside white rice.

name: Opor Ayam
description: A mild, creamy Javanese chicken stew in coconut milk and fragrant spices, traditionally served at Eid.
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, coriander, white pepper and turmeric to a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the paste with the galangal, bruised lemongrass, bay and lime leaves for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat, cooking 5 minutes.
Pour in the water and half the coconut milk, bring to a gentle boil, then simmer covered 25 minutes.
Stir in the remaining coconut milk, palm sugar and salt, and simmer uncovered 8 minutes without boiling hard.
Scatter with fried shallots and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Opor tastes even better the next day once the spices settle.
photo: Pieces of chicken in a pale creamy yellow coconut sauce in a clay bowl, topped with fried shallots and herbs.

name: Murtabak
description: A thin, crisp pan-fried flatbread packed with spiced minced beef, onion and egg, served with a sweet pickle.
steps: Knead the flour, water, 1 teaspoon salt and 1 tablespoon ghee into a soft dough for 5 minutes, divide into 4 balls, coat with ghee and rest 1 hour.
Fry one chopped onion, the garlic and ginger in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, add the beef and curry powder and cook 8 minutes until dry and browned; season with salt.
Cool the beef, then mix with the sliced spring onions and the second onion, finely chopped, and the beaten eggs (one egg per murtabak, keep separate).
Stretch one dough ball paper thin on an oiled surface into a large square.
Spoon a quarter of the filling and one beaten egg on the centre, then fold the sides over to make a sealed square parcel.
Fry in a little oil over medium heat for 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp and the egg is set.
Make a quick pickle by mixing sliced cucumber with vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Cut the murtabak into squares and serve hot with the pickle.
tips: Stretch the dough gently; thin spots are fine, tears are not.
photo: A golden crisp square murtabak cut into pieces showing the minced beef and egg filling, with a small bowl of cucumber pickle.

name: Beef Massaman Curry
description: Slow-cooked beef in a mild, aromatic coconut curry with potatoes, peanuts and warm spices.
steps: Cut the beef into 4 cm chunks and wedge the onions.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat, add the thick top half of the coconut milk and fry the curry paste 4 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the beef and stir 5 minutes to coat and brown lightly.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the water, add the cinnamon, cardamom and bay leaves, bring to a simmer and cook covered on low heat for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and onions and cook 25 minutes until the beef and potatoes are tender.
Stir in the fish sauce, palm sugar, tamarind and peanuts, simmer 5 minutes and taste to balance sweet, sour and salty.
Serve with jasmine rice.
tips: A pressure cooker cuts the beef cooking time to 35 minutes.
photo: Tender beef chunks and potatoes in a creamy orange-brown curry in a ceramic bowl, topped with roasted peanuts, rice alongside.

name: Thai Green Chicken Curry
description: A fragrant and creamy green curry with chicken, aubergine and Thai basil.
steps: Slice the chicken into bite-size pieces and cut the aubergines into wedges.
Heat the oil in a wok or pot over medium heat, add the curry paste and 200 ml of the thick coconut milk, and fry 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir for 4 minutes until it changes colour.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the water, add lime leaves, and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Add the aubergines and beans and cook 6 minutes until tender.
Stir in the fish sauce and palm sugar, taste and adjust, then add the basil and sliced chilli.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
tips: Use less paste for children and add chilli at the table.
photo: A bowl of pale green curry with chicken, round aubergines and green basil leaves, with a mound of white rice beside it.

name: Chicken Piaparan
description: A Maranao chicken stew in coconut milk with toasted grated coconut and palapa, a spicy spring-onion relish.
steps: Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 minutes until deep brown, then grind it into a rough paste.
Pound or blend half the spring onions, chillies, ginger and turmeric into a coarse palapa relish.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the chopped onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and brown on all sides for 6 minutes, then stir in the palapa and cook 2 minutes.
Add the water, lemongrass and half the coconut milk, cover and simmer 25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the toasted coconut, remaining coconut milk, salt and sugar and cook 5 minutes uncovered.
Top with the rest of the sliced spring onions and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Toasted coconut gives the sauce its nutty, dark colour; do not skip it.
photo: Chicken pieces in a thick brownish coconut sauce in a shallow bowl, topped with fresh green spring onion and red chilli slices.

name: Chicken Teriyaki
description: Pan-seared chicken thighs glazed in a glossy sweet-savoury soy sauce, served over rice.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, honey, sugar, apple juice, rice vinegar, grated ginger, crushed garlic and cornflour in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and place the chicken skin-side down.
Cook 6 minutes until the skin is golden, flip and cook 5 minutes more until almost cooked through.
Steam or boil the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright green and tender.
Pour the sauce into the pan, lower the heat to medium and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, turning the chicken, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Slice the chicken, spoon the sauce over and serve on rice with the broccoli.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.
tips: Take the chicken out of the fridge 15 minutes before cooking for even browning.
photo: Sliced glossy dark-glazed chicken fanned over a bowl of white rice with bright green broccoli and sesame seeds.

name: Beef Bulgogi
description: Thinly sliced beef marinated in a sweet pear and soy sauce, quickly seared and served with rice and lettuce wraps.
steps: Grate the pear and mix it with the soy sauce, sugar, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, crushed garlic, ginger and pepper.
Add the sliced beef, toss well and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour, up to overnight.
Slice the onion into half moons and the spring onions into 3 cm lengths.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or cast iron skillet over high heat.
Cook the beef in two batches for 2 to 3 minutes each, with the onion, until browned and caramelised at the edges.
Stir in the spring onions and sesame seeds, cook 30 seconds.
Serve with rice and lettuce leaves for wrapping.
tips: Freeze the beef for 30 minutes before slicing to get paper-thin pieces.
photo: Caramelised dark beef slices with onion and sesame seeds in a dish, with a bowl of rice and fresh green lettuce leaves beside.

name: Cumin Lamb Stir-Fry
description: Fiery Northwest Chinese stir-fry of sliced lamb with toasted cumin, chilli and fresh coriander.
steps: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant, then crush them coarsely.
Toss the lamb with the soy sauce, cornflour and half the crushed cumin and marinate 15 minutes.
Slice the onion, green chillies, garlic and spring onions.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over very high heat until smoking and sear the lamb for 2 minutes without moving, then stir-fry 1 more minute; remove.
Add the remaining oil and fry the onion, garlic and green chillies for 2 minutes.
Return the lamb and add the chilli flakes, Sichuan pepper, salt and remaining cumin, tossing for 1 minute.
Stir in the spring onions and coriander and serve at once with rice or flatbread.
tips: Work in small batches on high heat so the lamb sears instead of stewing.
photo: Browned lamb slices flecked with cumin and red chilli, with green chilli, onion and coriander on a dark plate.

name: Pisang Goreng (Banana Fritters)
description: Crisp golden battered bananas fried until caramelised and soft inside, a classic street snack.
steps: Whisk the plain flour, rice flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and turmeric in a bowl.
Gradually whisk in the cold water to make a smooth batter the thickness of single cream.
Peel the bananas and cut each in half lengthways, or in thirds if small.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat to about 170 C (a drop of batter should sizzle and rise).
Dip each banana piece in the batter, let the excess drip off, and lower into the oil.
Fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
tips: Use firm, just-ripe bananas such as plantain or pisang raja for best results.
photo: A pile of golden crunchy banana fritters on a rustic plate lined with paper, with a few banana slices showing soft yellow inside.

name: Klepon (Palm Sugar Rice Balls)
description: Chewy pandan-green glutinous rice balls that burst with liquid palm sugar, rolled in fresh coconut.
steps: Mix the glutinous rice flour with the pandan juice and warm water, kneading to a soft dough that does not crack.
Chop or grate the palm sugar into small pieces.
Pinch off walnut-sized pieces of dough, flatten each, place a piece of palm sugar in the middle and seal into a smooth ball.
Bring the water to a boil in a large pot over high heat.
Drop in the balls in batches and cook 3 to 4 minutes until they float, then 1 more minute.
Meanwhile steam the grated coconut with the salt for 10 minutes.
Lift the balls out with a slotted spoon, drain well and roll them in the coconut.
Serve at room temperature.
tips: Seal the balls well or the sugar will leak out while boiling.
photo: Small bright green round balls rolled in white shredded coconut, piled on a banana leaf lined plate.
